findings.evidence: 'Specific and scannable (5-8 words ideal)', 'Bullets for multiple points (3-5 max)', and 'Short paragraphs (2-3 sentences max)' exemplify the lengthy Workflow section's standard email-writing advice. The body adds little expert-only knowledge beyond brief activation and formatting instructions.
findings.fix: Compress the familiar writing advice into a short checklist. Replace the tutorial material with concrete, experience-derived engineering communication conventions for incident uncertainty, release-risk disclosure, and scope-versus-deadline negotiations.

findings.evidence: 'Email Purpose' offers status updates, requests, information sharing, escalations, and follow-ups, but every purpose proceeds directly to the same 'What-Why-How' structure without criteria for choosing the evidence or reasoning each purpose needs.
findings.fix: Add a brief purpose-based decision step: status updates establish impact and confidence; requests identify the exact decision and constraints; escalations compare options and recommend an owner or intervention. Then apply the shared drafting framework.

findings.evidence: 'Anti-Patterns to Avoid' lists familiar warnings such as 'Wall of text without structure', 'Missing clear call-to-action', and 'CC’ing unnecessarily', without explaining consequences or documenting non-obvious gotchas.
findings.fix: Replace or supplement these warnings with specific prohibitions and reasons: never turn uncertain estimates into commitments, because recipients may treat them as approved dates; never imply an incident root cause is confirmed when only a hypothesis exists; never copy internal incident details into an external-facing draft without checking disclosure scope.

findings.evidence: 'Email body with WHAT/WHY/HOW sections labeled' requires visible process labels for every email, while the framework also prescribes opening and context sentence counts regardless of message complexity.
findings.fix: Make What-Why-How an internal drafting heuristic. Default to a copy-ready email without framework labels, allow short messages to omit unnecessary background, and use explicit headings only for longer messages or when requested.

findings.evidence: Reading commands/evals/compose-email.json returned ENOENT; commands/evals/ contains explain-pr-changes.json and files/, but no compose-email eval.
findings.fix: Add commands/evals/compose-email.json with realistic prompts, expected outputs, and verifiable assertions covering a complete request, refinement of an existing draft, an empty-context invocation, and an FYI or escalation edge case. Check preservation of supplied facts and absence of invented deadlines or commitments.

findings.evidence: 'If $ARGUMENTS is empty or insufficient, use AskUserQuestion to gather' leads only to Audience, Purpose, and Urgency questions. With empty arguments, those answers still do not establish the actual topic, facts, or requested outcome before Step 4 generates a complete email.
findings.fix: Ask first for the actual message or situation, essential facts, and desired recipient outcome; ask only for remaining missing details afterward. If clarification cannot be obtained, provide explicitly marked placeholders or ask a plain-text follow-up instead of inventing content.

findings.evidence: All three examples invoke '/soft-skills:draft-email', including '/soft-skills:draft-email Need to ask team lead for deadline extension on API migration', but this file defines the command stem compose-email, not draft-email.
findings.fix: Update all three examples to invoke /compose-email, or the verified plugin-qualified command whose command component is compose-email, and retain examples for contextual drafting, draft refinement, and starting without arguments.
